annotations.title: God wil circumcise thy hart.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> Most true it is, that of our selues, without Gods grace none can kepe or fulfil the commandmentes. But he, whose hart God doth circumcise, is therby made able to loue God with al his hart, and with al his soule. And except some hartes were thus circumcised, and so made able to loue God aboue al, and consequently their neighboures, God should not performe his promise, that he wil circumcise the hart of some.

notes.text: By grace men are made able to kepe Gods commandments

annotations.title: Is not aboue thee.
annotations.text: [1] VVhen thou art stirred vp, assisted, and indued with Gods grace, [2]the commandment of God is not (then) aboue thee, nor farre of from thee, but very nere thee, in thy mouth (to confesse God, and his truth) and in thy hart, to do it. But you wil aske: How then cometh it to passe, that manie hauing receiued sufficient grace, yet do not kepe Gods commandmentes? God him self answereth: 15. That he hath set before thee life and good, and contrriwise death and euil; he inuiteth and helpeth, yet forceth thee not: he geueth thee powre & abilitie, helping and not destroying thy freewil, that thou maist loue our Lord thy God, walke in his wayes, and kepe his commandements. But if thy hart be auerted and (v. 17.) thou wilt not heare, thou shalt perish. Againe God inculcateth: 19. I cal for witnesses heauen and earth, that I haue proposed to you life and death, blessing and cursing. Choose therfore life &c. VVhat Doctor can teach more plainly the possibilitie of keeping Gods commandmentes; and frewil in man, then this text of holie Scripture?

notes.text: So the commandmentes are not impossible.
S. Aug. de nat. et grat. c. 69. et q. 54. in Deut. Theod. q. 38. in Deut. S. Cypr. l. 3. c. 52. ad Quir. S. Amb. in Psal. 40.

But if thy heart be averted and (v. 17.) thou wilt not hear, thou shalt perish. Again, God inculcateth:
